messages:
Mira: Heads-up — ~09:12 UTC we saw a sharp latency bump for model-serving in asia-east1 after a ~30% spot eviction wave. Traffic recovered slowly; lots of 502s that align with ImagePullBackOff and kubelet backlog. Anyone else seeing the same pattern?
Sam: saw it. 502s started when autoscaler spun up a bunch of nodes at once, image pulls saturated our registry egress and pods timed out. Scale rate looked ~20 nodes/min.
Ivy: cc @chen — our rollout was also concurrent which made the pulls spike. Logs show many nodes stuck in ContainerCreating for several minutes.
Chen: confirmed. deploy-bot scaled gpu-asia-spot-pool 120 -> 210 in ~8m. Registry egress hit 78% of quota and kubelet retries piled up.
deploy-bot: action: scaled gpu-asia-spot-pool replicaCount=210 reason="eviction-wave detected"
Mira: Proposal: avoid an all-in scale burst. Ideas: keep a small warm-on-demand buffer (tainted), prefer those nodes, and limit autoscaler scale-rate to 10 nodes/min with a 3m provision cooldown between steps. That should reduce image-pull concurrency and registry pressure. Thoughts? :thinking:
Leo: +1. Also reduce concurrent DaemonSet startup churn (node-exporter, logging) during scale bursts. We can set pod startup surge to stagger hooks.
Sam: Another concrete lever: pre-pull images to warm nodes via a simple job rather than pulling in parallel on new nodes. e.g. run an image-warm job in infra namespace that keeps layers cached.
Ivy: runtime-level optimization too: prefix/KV cache warming would let the service respond from memcache while pods finish init, but that needs infra+runtime changes.
Chen: operational alternative: a small dedicated on-demand nodepool annotated for warm capacity and tainted (warm=true:NoSchedule). Set critical workloads to tolerate that taint. During eviction waves the autoscaler can first claim those nodes. Safer than instant on-demand scale.
Mira: Config suggestion for PR: autoscaler.maxScaleRate=10/min, autoscaler.provisionCooldown=180s, cluster.spotWarmupBufferPct=8 (percent of q95 qps). Can someone sketch the PR?
Ivy: I'll open a draft PR to eng-infra/cluster-config adding spotWarmupBuffer and provisionCooldown fields plus a unit test for the scale rate enforcement.
Sam: Test plan: run chaos sim in staging that evicts 35% of spot GPUs across zones, measure time to steady QPS and count ImagePullBackOffs. We'll vary warm buffer sizes (0, 5%, 10%) and scaleRate caps.
Chen: Also log action: I'll dig into registry metrics and propose a regional caching plan (Artifact Registry mirrors) — we saw cross-zone egress spikes that probably exacerbated the problem.
Leo: K8s command snippet to create a tainted warm pool for staging if people want to try locally: 
```
gcloud container node-pools create warm-on-demand --cluster=ci-cluster --region=asia-east1 --machine-type=a2-highgpu-1g --node-taints=warm=true:NoSchedule --num-nodes=6
```
Mira: action items: Ivy -> PR for autoscaler cooldown + warm buffer config; Sam -> chaos sim matrix and run; Chen -> registry egress analysis & caching proposal; Leo -> provision warm nodepool in staging and run pre-pull job; Mira -> monitor tonight and collect traces. Reconvene in ~24h. :thumbsup:
Sam: noted, will add the test matrix to the ticket.
Ivy: PR draft: <https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/compare/draft-spot-warmup> (draft, WIP).
Mira: thanks all — if anyone needs access to the staging cluster for the sim ping me.
Chen: +1 on staging access, will ping.
Leo: I'll run the pre-pull job after the warm pool is up.
Mira: closing loop — keep the thread updated with sim results.
